1. Area of the base = $\pi r^2$
2. Area of the curved surface = perimeter of the base $\times$ height = $2\pi rh$
3. Area of the whole surface = $(\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh + \pi r^2) = 2\pi r(r + h)$
4. Volume = Area of the base $\times$ height = $\pi r^2h$

Example 30. If the height of a right circular cylinder is $10\text{ cm}$ and radius of the base is $7\text{ cm}$, determine its volume and the area of the whole surface.

Solution: Let, the height of the right circular cylinder is $h = 10\text{ cm}$ and radius of the base is $r$.

$\therefore$ Its volume = $\pi r^2h$
$= 3.1416 \times 7^2 \times 10 = 1539.38\text{ cube cm (approx.)}$

and the area of the whole surface = $2\pi r(r + h)$
$= 2 \times 3.1416 \times 7(7 + 10) = 747.7\text{ square metre (approx.)}$
Work: Make a right circular cylinder using a rectangular paper. Determine the area of its whole surface and the volume.

Example 31. The outer measurements of a box with its top are $10\text{ cm}$, $9\text{ cm}$ and $7\text{ cm}$ respectively and the area of the whole inner surface is $262\text{ square metre}$ and the thickness of its wall is uniform on all sides.

1) Find the volume of the box.
2) Find the thickness of its wall.
3) If the length of a diagonal of a rhombus having sides equal to the largest length of the box is $16\text{ cm}$, then find its area.

Solution:
1) The outer measurements of the box with top are $10\text{ cm}$, $9\text{ cm}$ and $7\text{ cm}$.
$\therefore$ The outer volume of the box = $10 \times 9 \times 7 = 630\text{ cube cm}$

2) Let, the thickness of the box is $x$. The outer measurements of the box with top are $10\text{ cm}$, $9\text{ cm}$, $7\text{ cm}$.
$\therefore$ The inside measurements of the box are respectively $a = (10 - 2x)$, $b = (9 - 2x)$ and $c = (7 - 2x)\text{ cm}$.
The area of the whole surface of the inner side of the box = $2(ab + bc + ca)$
